extracted.intended_audience: readers/subscribers of Herbert Spencer's philosophical series; Victorian-era educated public; librarians and scholars of philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Outline and publication/programme for Herbert Spencer's planned multi-volume philosophical series (First Principles, Principles of Biology, Psychology, Sociology, Morality) together with Google Books usage notes for the digital copy. The page sets out the intended contents of each part/volume and practical usage/distribution guidance for the scanned edition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make non-commercial use of the files
rubrics_metrics.description: We designed Google Book Search for use by individuals, and we request that you use these files for personal, non-commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit request by Google that the scanned public-domain book files be used for personal, non-commercial purposes to prevent commercial abuse of the digitized public-domain materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refrain from automated querying
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not send automated queries of any sort to Google's system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conducting research requiring large amounts of text (e.g., machine translation, OCR research), contact Google for access; Google encourages such research and may be able to help. Google also places technical restrictions on automated querying to prevent abuse by commercial parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain attribution / Do not remove Google watermark
rubrics_metrics.description: The Google 'watermark' you see on each file is essential for informing people about this project and helping them find additional materials through Google Book Search. Please do not remove it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The watermark is considered essential attribution for the digitized file; removal is explicitly discouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep it legal / verify public-domain status in your jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: You are responsible for ensuring that what you are doing is legal; do not assume that a book is public domain in every country because it is in Google Book Search for the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Google disclaims the ability to offer guidance on whether any specific use of any specific book is allowed in other jurisdictions; users must verify copyright status themselves because public-domain status may vary country to country.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Principles — Part I: The Unknowable
rubrics_metrics.description: Carrying a step further the doctrine put into shape by Hamilton and Mansel; pointing out the various directions in which Science leads to the same conclusions; and showing that in this united belief in an Absolute that transcends not only human knowledge but human conception, lies the only possible reconciliation of Science and Religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part I treats the Unknowable and the reconciliation of Science and Religion via the concept of an Absolute transcending knowledge and conception.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Principles — Part II: Laws of the Knowable
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the ultimate principles discernible throughout all manifestations of the Absolute — those highest generalizations now being disclosed by Science which are severally true not of one class of phenomena but of all classes of phenomena; and which are thus the keys to all classes of phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part II aims to state the ultimate general principles (e.g., conservation of force and related generalizations) that apply across phenomena and serve as keys to interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Biology — Vol. I, Part I: The Data of Biology
rubrics_metrics.description: Including those general truths of Physics and Chemistry with which rational Biology must set out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This part collects necessary physical and chemical truths as the starting data for a rational treatment of biology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Biology — Vol. I, Part II: The Inductions of Biology
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the leading generalizations which Naturalists, Physiologists, and Comparative Anatomists have established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digest of empirically established generalizations across biological disciplines to underpin further theorizing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Biology — Vol. I, Part III: The Evolution of Life
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerning the speculation commonly known as 'The Development Hypothesis' — its a priori and a posteriori evidences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines the development hypothesis (evolution) and both theoretical and empirical evidence supporting it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Biology — Vol. II, Part IV: Morphological Development
rubrics_metrics.description: Pointing out the relations that are everywhere traceable between organic forms and the average of the various forces to which they are subject; and seeking in the cumulative effects of such forces a theory of the forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on how form arises from the interaction of forces and conditions; morphological theory based on cumulative forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Biology — Vol. II, Part V: Physiological Development
rubrics_metrics.description: The progressive differentiation of functions similarly traced; and similarly interpreted as consequent upon the exposure of different parts of organisms to different sets of conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interprets functional differentiation as arising from differential exposure to conditions; links physiology to external conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Biology — Vol. II, Part VI: The Laws of Multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalizations respecting the rates of reproduction of the various classes of plants and animals; followed by an attempt to show the dependence of these variations upon certain necessary causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discusses reproductive rate laws and attempts to correlate variations with necessary causal factors (reference to earlier papers including 'Theory of Population').

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. I, Part I: The Data of Psychology
rubrics_metrics.description: Treating of the general connexions of Mind and Life and their relations to other modes of the Unknowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the basic data relating mind and life and situates them with respect to the Unknowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. I, Part II: The Inductions of Psychology
rubrics_metrics.description: A digest of such generalizations respecting mental phenomena as have already been empirically established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects empirically established generalizations about mental phenomena to form the induction base.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. I, Part III: General Synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: A republication, with additional chapters, of the same part in the already-published Principles of Psychology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Synthesis stage consolidating prior published material with additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. I, Part IV: Special Synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: A republication, with extensive revisions and additions, of the same part, &c. &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further synthesis with substantial revision and new material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. I, Part V: Physical Synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: An attempt to show the manner in which the succession of states of consciousness conforms to a certain fundamental law of nervous action that follows from the First Principles laid down at the outset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connects states of consciousness to a law of nervous action derivable from the First Principles; attempts physical explanatory synthesis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. II, Part VI: Special Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: As at present published, but further elaborated by some additional chapters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further analytical development and elaboration of previously published analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. II, Part VII: General Analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: As at present published, with several explanations and additions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad analysis with clarifying additions; builds on previously published work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Psychology — Vol. II, Part VIII: Corollaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Consisting in part of a number of derivative principles which form a necessary introduction to Sociology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derivative principles intended to bridge psychology and sociology; prepares ground for sociological theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. I, Part I: The Data of Sociology
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement of the several sets of factors entering into social phenomena — human ideas and feelings considered in their necessary order of evolution; surrounding natural conditions; and those ever complicating conditions to which Society itself gives origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects the multiple factors relevant to social phenomena, including human psychology, natural conditions, and society-created conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. I, Part II: The Inductions of Sociology
rubrics_metrics.description: General facts, structural and functional, as gathered from a survey of Societies and their changes: in other words, the empirical generalizations arrived at by comparing different societies, and successive phases of the same society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirical generalizations about social structures/functions based on comparative and historical study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. I, Part III: Political Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The evolution of governments, general and local, as determined by natural causes; their several types and metamorphoses; their increasing complexity and specialization; and the progressive limitation of their sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analysis of governmental evolution, types, specialization, and limits on sanctions; treatment of political organization as a natural-historical phenomenon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. II, Part IV: Ecclesiastical Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: Tracing the differentiation of religious government from secular; its successive complications and the multiplication of sects; the growth and continued modification of religious ideas, as caused by advancing knowledge and changing moral character; and the gradual reconciliation of these ideas with the truths of abstract science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on the historical differentiation and development of religious institutions and ideas, their sectarian multiplication, and reconciliation with scientific truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. II, Part V: Ceremonial Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural history of that third kind of government which, having a common root with the others, and slowly becoming separate from and supplementary to them, serves to regulate the minor actions of life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies ceremonial institutions as a distinct organizational type regulating everyday life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. II, Part VI: Industrial Organization
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of productive and distributive agencies, considered, like the foregoing, in its necessary causes: comprehending not only the progressive division of labour, and the increasing complexity of each industrial agency, but also the successive forms of industrial government as passing through like phases with political government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines industrial development, division of labour, complexity, and parallels between industrial and political organizational evolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. III, Part VII: Lingual Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The evolution of Languages regarded as a psychological process determined by social conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treats language evolution as driven by social-psychological factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. III, Part VIII: Intellectual Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Treated from the same point of view: including the growth of classifications; the evolution of science out of common knowledge; the advance from qualitive to quantative prevision, from the indefinite to the definite, and from the concrete to the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyzes intellectual development from social conditions; covers classification growth, scientific evolution, and conceptual abstraction trends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. III, Part IX: Esthetic Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: The Fine Arts similarly dealt with: tracing their gradual differentiation from primitive institutions and from each other; their increasing varieties of development; and their advance in reality of expression and superiority of aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Studies the evolution and differentiation of the fine arts and their progressive refinement and aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Sociology — Vol. III, Part X: Moral Progress
rubrics_metrics.description: Exhibiting the genesis of the slow emotional modifications which human nature undergoes in its adaptation to the social state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examines emotional and moral modifications during social adaptation and development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Morality — Part I: The Data of Morality
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalizations furnished by Biology, Psychology and Sociology, which underlie a true theory of right living: in other words, the elements of that equilibrium between constitution and conditions of existence, which is at once the moral ideal and the limit towards which we are progressing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collects cross-disciplinary generalizations to ground a theory of morality based on equilibrium between constitution and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Morality — Part II: The Inductions of Morality
rubrics_metrics.description: Those empirically-established rules of human action which are registered as essential laws by all civilized nations: that is to say — the generalizations of expediency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presents empirically established rules of action (expediency) recognized across civilized societies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Morality — Part III: Personal Morals
rubrics_metrics.description: The principles of private conduct — physical, intellectual, moral and religious — that follow from the conditions to complete individual life: or, what is the same thing — those modes of private action which must result from the eventual equilibration of internal desires and external needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Derives principles of private conduct from the equilibrium of internal desires and external needs; covers multiple dimensions of personal life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Morality — Vol. II, Part IV: Justice
rubrics_metrics.description: The mutual limitations of men's actions necessitated by their co-existence as units of a society — limitations, the perfect observance of which constitutes that state of equilibrium forming the goal of political progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyzes justice as mutual limitation necessary for social co-existence and political progress toward equilibrium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Morality — Vol. II, Part V: Negative Beneficence
rubrics_metrics.description: Those secondary limitations, similarly necessitated, which, though less important and not cognizable by law, are yet requisite to prevent mutual destruction of happiness in various indirect ways: in other words — those minor self-restraints dictated by what may be called passive sympathy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on secondary, informal restraints (passive sympathy) that preserve mutual happiness but are not legally enforceable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles of Morality — Vol. II, Part VI: Positive Beneficence
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehending all modes of conduct, dictated by active sympathy, which imply pleasure in giving pleasure — modes of conduct that social adaptation has produced, and must render ever more general; and which, in becoming universal, must fill to the full the possible measure of human happiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considers active sympathetic conduct (positive beneficence) as socially produced and progressively generalizable to maximize human happiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programme — scope and limits: establish principles with illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: An exhaustive treatment of each topic is not intended; the aim is simply the establishment of principles, with such illustrations as are needed to make their bearings fully understood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author explicitly limits the ambition of each part to establishing principles and providing necessary illustrations rather than exhaustive treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication plan / subscription terms
rubrics_metrics.description: The price per Number to be half-a-crown; the four Numbers yearly issued to be severally delivered post free to all annual subscribers of Ten Shillings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical publication/distribution detail indicating planned frequency, pricing per number, and annual subscription rate.
